filename: The importance of adding unbiased Argo observations to the ocean carbon observing system.pdf
title: The importance of adding unbiased Argo observations to the ocean carbon observing system
testbed_rationale: The Large Ensemble Testbed (LET) is designed for assessing observational sampling networks and machine learning reconstruction/gap-filling of surface ocean carbon fields rather than training or evaluating subgrid parameterizations or emulators.
pain_points: Severe spatial and temporal gaps in direct shipboard surface ocean pCO2 observations (SOCAT covers ~2% of the ocean).
Float-derived pCO2 carries substantial random uncertainty (±11 µatm) and systematic positive bias (~4 µatm).

Systematic observational bias in autonomous float observations propagates strongly through machine learning models, causing substantial underestimation of the global ocean carbon sink (up to 0.32 Pg C/year).
Cross-model structural differences across Earth System Models introduce significant spread in machine learning reconstruction skill.
extraction_notes: The research was funded by NSF through the LEAP STC (Award #2019625). The target variable is pCO2-Residual, reconstructed from sea surface temperature (SST), sea surface salinity (SSS), atmospheric xCO2, mixed layer depth (MLD), and chlorophyll-a.
